standard_prerequisites.name: Whiskering and composition of natural transformations
standard_prerequisites.statement: delta G and H gamma denote the whiskered composites of a natural transformation with a functor.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two sides of the interchange identity.

standard_prerequisites.name: Componentwise equality of natural transformations
standard_prerequisites.statement: Two natural transformations are equal as soon as their components are equal at every object.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the reduction performed at the start of the proof.

core_obligations: Reduce the identity of natural transformations to the componentwise statement at an arbitrary object a : A (source line 422).
Unfold the two composites at a to obtain the chain delta_{Ga} o H(gamma_a) on one side (source lines 424-426).
Apply the naturality of delta to replace delta_{Ga} o H(gamma_a) by K(gamma_a) o delta_{Fa} (source line 427).
Recognise the result as the component at a of (K gamma)(delta F) and conclude the interchange identity (source lines 428-429).

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce to components and unfold both composites.
Identify the result with the other composite.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 9.2.8 at source lines 416-420: for functors F, G : A -> B and H, K : B -> C with natural transformations gamma : F -> G and delta : H -> K, the two composites (delta G)(H gamma) and (K gamma)(delta F) are equal. The author's proof (source lines 421-431) is a componentwise chase: after reducing to the component at an object a (line 422) it unfolds both whiskered composites (lines 424-426), and the single non-definitional step is the application of the naturality of delta at the component gamma_a (line 427), after which the two sides are seen to be the same displayed expression (lines 428-429). The statement is one identity between natural transformations and records neither the componentwise reduction nor which naturality square is used.
